title: Staff didn't stop Geldart from leaving psychiatric ward, inquest hears
article: Kevin Geldart promised staff in Moncton Hospital's psychiatric ward he'd only be gone 15 minutes the night he died, an inquest heard Thursday.
Geldart, 34, died on May 5, 2005, after police subdued him with a taser gun in a Moncton bar.
Psychiatric attendant Henry Surrette testified Thursday that Geldart, who was not allowed to the leave the floor, walked by the ward's nurse's station at about 9 p.m. that night.
Surrette said the man's six-foot-six-inch, 350-pound frame was a familiar one and easy to spot. The attendant said he asked Geldart where he was going.

Surrette testified that Geldart told him he wanted a cigarette. Geldart was already close to the exit, and Surette testified that there wasn't much he could do to stopGeldart from leaving. He promised to come back in 15 minutes, Surrette said.
Head nurse Susan Laurette testified that when Geldart didn't return at 9:30 p.m., she notified security, as well as the RCMP, because Geldart was an involuntary patient.
Later that evening, the staff learned that Geldart had died.
Surrette and Laurette testified psychiatric patients are constantly going outside to smoke and it's hard to keep track of them.
Dr. Dinesh Bhalla, the last psychiatrist to treat Geldart in the hospital, also testified Thursday.
Bhalla said Geldart was hospitalized seven times during his struggle with bipolar disorder.
Bhalla said a community treatment order within the Mental Health Act would help make treatment for patients like Geldart more consistent.

"They are a contract between a patient and his doctor ... to ensure that they are going to follow up with the doctor in their office and also going to ensure that they're going to see their mental health workers on a regular basis."
Bhalla said the government could make them mandatory through a change in the Mental Health Act.
The inquest into Geldart's death is scheduled to run until March 2.
